scales.alcohol: 1 low, 2 medium(-), 3 medium, 4 medium(+), 5 high; for still wines roughly under 11%, 11 to 12, 12 to 13.5, 13.5 to 14, over 14% abv (project convention; WSET SAT 2022 gives no thresholds); fortified wines are judged on their own low/medium/high scale

styles.sweet: sweet (late harvest, dried grape, icewine, passito)
styles.oxidative: oxidative or biologically aged (vin jaune, oloroso, Rutherglen)

_meta.variant_styles: A style key with a suffix (e.g. white_oaked, red_warm, white_rich, red_dried) is a second profile of the same base style; its base is given in 'base' and a human label in 'label'.
_meta.colour: Each entry is '<intensity> <hue>' from the WSET SAT: intensity pale/medium/deep; hue lemon-green, lemon, gold, amber, brown (white); pink, salmon, orange (rosé); purple, ruby, garnet, tawny, brown (red).
_meta.clusters: Aroma descriptors are grouped by WSET Level 3 Wine-Lexicon clusters (primary: floral, green fruit, citrus fruit, stone fruit, tropical fruit, red fruit, black fruit, dried/cooked fruit, herbaceous, herbal, pungent spice, other; secondary: yeast, malolactic conversion, oak; tertiary: deliberate oxidation, fruit development, bottle age). Project extensions: carbonic maceration, noble rot, fortification, skin contact.
_meta.coverage: 250 of 266 grape ids. Omitted (collection, table-grape or extinct vines with no current wine style): magdeleine-noire-des-charentes, gros-cabernet, gouais-blanc, dureza, mondeuse-blanche, peloursin, calabrese-di-montenuovo, benedicto, heben, castellana-blanca, madeleine-royale, st-georgener-rebe, blaue-zimmettraube, kyoho, heptakilo, rayon-d-or.
_meta.method: Ranges synthesise the WSET Level 3 SAT scales and the classic markers taught in WSET Diploma and CMS deductive tasting with variety descriptions in Robinson, Harding and Vouillamoz (Wine Grapes) and producer and consortium specifications. Where sources disagree the range is widened rather than averaged. These are typical ranges for classic examples, not limits.

cabernet-sauvignon.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
cabernet-sauvignon.markers: Blackcurrant, cedar, graphite and green capsicum; deep colour; high tannin and high acid; long finish.

red.oak: Almost always oak-aged: 18 to 24 months in 225 l barriques, 40 to 100% new for top Bordeaux and Napa; French oak for cedar and spice, American oak for coconut and dill in parts of Australia, Rioja-influenced Spain and older Napa.
red.markers: Deep colour, high tannin and medium+ to high acid even when ripe; cassis, cedar and leafy or capsicum notes from methoxypyrazines when cool or underripe; tannin builds on the finish.

classic_regions.name: Pauillac
classic_regions.markers: Cassis, cedar and graphite on a firm, fine-grained frame; 12.5 to 14% abv; medium+ body; decades of ageing. The benchmark Left Bank blend, 60 to 90% Cabernet.

classic_regions.name: Margaux
classic_regions.markers: The most perfumed Médoc: violets, red and black fruit, finer and silkier tannin than Pauillac on thin gravel.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Estèphe
classic_regions.markers: More clay in the gravel: firmer, more austere tannin and higher acid, often more Merlot; slower to open.

classic_regions.name: Napa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Riper black fruit, cassis liqueur and mocha, 14.5 to 15.5% abv, full body, lower acid (often adjusted), plush ripe tannin, lavish new French oak.

classic_regions.name: Rutherford
classic_regions.markers: Rutherford dust: dusty, cocoa-tinged tannin with black cherry and sage on the western bench.

classic_regions.name: Coonawarra
classic_regions.markers: Terra rossa over limestone: cassis with a distinct mint and eucalyptus lift, medium+ acid, firm but not heavy.

classic_regions.name: Margaret River
classic_regions.markers: Maritime Cabernet: elegant, cassis and bay leaf with a herbal edge, fine tannin, Bordeaux-like structure.

classic_regions.name: Valle del Maipo
classic_regions.markers: Alto Maipo (Puente Alto, Pirque): cassis with mint and dusty earth, ripe fruit with an Andean freshness.

classic_regions.name: Bolgheri
classic_regions.markers: Coastal Tuscan blend: ripe black fruit, Mediterranean herbs, polished tannin; Sassicaia (1968) is the model.

classic_regions.name: Stellenbosch
classic_regions.markers: Blackcurrant with a savoury, smoky and graphite edge, medium+ to high acid from mountain sites such as the Helderberg and Simonsberg.

classic_regions.name: Red Mountain
classic_regions.markers: Washington power: dense, high-tannin Cabernet from the hottest Yakima Valley site, with bright acid from cold nights.

confused_with.tell: Franc is lighter in colour and body, with more red fruit, violets and leafy, graphite notes and less tannin.
Merlot has rounder, softer mid-palate, plum and fruitcake fruit, lower acid and less drying tannin.
Carmenère shows stronger pyrazine (green pepper, jalapeño), softer tannin, lower acid and dark chocolate.

merlot.name: Merlot
merlot.markers: Plum and fruitcake, chocolate and mocha from oak, round soft mid-palate, medium acid, medium+ but ripe tannin.

red.oak: Top Right Bank and Italian examples age 12 to 24 months in French barriques, often a high share new; everyday Merlot sees chips, staves or none.
red.markers: Plush, round mid-palate; medium acid; medium+ but softer tannin than Cabernet; plum and fruitcake; chocolate and mocha from oak.

classic_regions.name: Pomerol
classic_regions.markers: Blue clay of the plateau: velvety, plush plum and black cherry, truffle with age, medium acid and fine, ripe tannin. Pétrus is about 100% Merlot.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Emilion grand cru
classic_regions.markers: Limestone plateau and côtes: fresher, more mineral Merlot blended with Cabernet Franc, firmer acid than Pomerol.

classic_regions.name: Bolgheri
classic_regions.markers: Masseto is the reference for Tuscan Merlot: dense, ripe and polished.

classic_regions.name: Napa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Rich, ripe and plummy, high alcohol and generous oak; Duckhorn helped build its 1980s reputation.

classic_regions.name: Walla Walla Valley
classic_regions.markers: Washington Merlot: dark fruit with brighter acid from the Columbia Valley diurnal shift.

classic_regions.name: Ticino
classic_regions.markers: Swiss Merlot from Ticino, often lighter and fresh, also vinified white (Merlot bianco).

classic_regions.name: Hawke's Bay
classic_regions.markers: Gimblett Gravels blends: ripe plum with fresh acid and moderate alcohol.

classic_regions.name: Bordeaux
classic_regions.markers: Bordeaux rosé and clairet: deeper-coloured, fruity, Merlot-dominant.

confused_with.tell: Cabernet has more acid and grippy tannin, cassis rather than plum, and a narrower, more linear frame.
Malbec is more purple, with violet, blueberry and a fleshier, sweeter fruit core.

cabernet-franc.name: Cabernet Franc
cabernet-franc.markers: Raspberry and violet, leafy and graphite notes, medium body, high acid, moderate tannin.

red.oak: Loire reds are often raised in large old foudres or tank; Saint-Émilion and top Loire cuvées use barriques.
red.markers: Medium body with high acid; leafy, red-fruited and floral; graphite and pencil-shavings; medium to medium+ tannin, less than Cabernet Sauvignon.

classic_regions.name: Chinon
classic_regions.markers: Raspberry, violet and pencil lead with a leafy, gravelly crunch; tuffeau-limestone slopes give longer-lived wines than the river gravels.

classic_regions.name: Bourgueil
classic_regions.markers: Firmer and darker than Chinon, more tannin, from the gravel terraces and tuffeau slopes north of the Loire.

classic_regions.name: Saumur-Champigny
classic_regions.markers: Juicy, supple, red-fruited and floral on tuffeau, the lightest of the trio.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Emilion grand cru
classic_regions.markers: Blended with Merlot for freshness, perfume and structure; Cheval Blanc is majority Cabernet Franc.

classic_regions.name: Napa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Riper, darker, oaked; increasingly bottled alone.

classic_regions.name: Valle de Uco
classic_regions.markers: Andean Cabernet Franc: bright acid, ripe red and black fruit, chalky tannin from limestone sites in Gualtallary and Paraje Altamira.

rose.markers: Raspberry fruit, often off-dry in Anjou.

classic_regions.name: Cabernet d'Anjou
classic_regions.markers: Off-dry to medium-dry, pink, raspberry-scented; must be at least 10 g/l sugar.

confused_with.tell: Sauvignon is deeper, more tannic and more black-fruited with cassis.
Pinot has no pyrazine leafiness, softer tannin and more cherry and forest-floor character.

carmenere.name: Carmenère
carmenere.markers: Green pepper and jalapeño, black fruit, dark chocolate, soft tannin, moderate acid.

red.oak: Usually oak-aged in French barriques for premium cuvées.
red.markers: Deep purple with magenta rim; strong pyrazine (green pepper, jalapeño, tomato leaf) even when ripe; soft, round tannin; medium acid; dark chocolate and spice.

classic_regions.name: Peumo
classic_regions.markers: The benchmark Carmenère site in Cachapoal: ripe black fruit and spice with less greenness; Concha y Toro Carmín de Peumo.

classic_regions.name: Valle de Colchagua
classic_regions.markers: Warm Apalta and Colchagua: rich, ripe, oaky with chocolate and soft tannin.

classic_regions.name: Valle del Maipo
classic_regions.markers: Fresher, herbal versions.

red.note: Belancic and Agosin (AJEV 2007) measured IBMP of 5.0 to 44.4 ng/l in Carmenère wines, much higher than most Cabernet Sauvignon.

confused_with.tell: Cabernet has firmer tannin and higher acid; Carmenère is greener and softer.
Merlot rarely shows so much pyrazine and has redder plum fruit.

malbec.name: Malbec
malbec.markers: Inky purple, violet and blueberry, plush ripe tannin and medium acid (Argentina); rustic, tannic, earthy (Cahors).

red.oak: Argentine reserves age 12 to 18 months in French oak; entry wines tank or old wood; Cahors in barrel or large foudres.
red.markers: Very deep purple with magenta rim; violet and blue-black fruit; medium+ body; medium acid; ripe, velvety tannin in Argentina, firmer in Cahors.

classic_regions.name: Luján de Cuyo
classic_regions.markers: Classic first zone (900 to 1,100 m): plush, ripe, plum and chocolate, soft tannin.

classic_regions.name: Valle de Uco
classic_regions.markers: Higher (1,000 to 1,500 m+): brighter acid, violet perfume, chalky tannin, fresher blue fruit; Gualtallary and Paraje Altamira lead.

classic_regions.name: Cafayate
classic_regions.markers: Salta altitude (1,700 m+): very deep colour, thick skins, intense spicy fruit and firm tannin.

classic_regions.name: Cahors
classic_regions.markers: The black wine of Cahors (min 70% Côt): firmer tannin, higher acid, more earth and less fruit than Argentina; limestone causses vs Lot terraces.

classic_regions.name: Mendoza
classic_regions.markers: Fruity, deep-pink rosado.

confused_with.tell: Syrah has pepper, olive and smoked meat; Malbec is more floral and fleshier.
Merlot is less purple and less floral, with plum and fruitcake.

petit-verdot.name: Petit Verdot
petit-verdot.markers: Opaque colour, violet, blueberry and sage, high tannin and acid.

red.oak: Typically oaked; in Bordeaux it is a 1 to 5% blending component.
red.markers: Opaque, violet and spice, very high tannin and acid; mostly a blender.

classic_regions.name: Margaux
classic_regions.markers: A few percent add colour, spice and backbone to Médoc blends (Palmer, Margaux).

classic_regions.name: Riverland
classic_regions.markers: Large warm-climate varietal plantings.

classic_regions.name: Virginia
classic_regions.markers: A Virginia speciality, ripening reliably in a humid climate.

sauvignon-blanc.name: Sauvignon Blanc
sauvignon-blanc.markers: Pronounced gooseberry, grapefruit, passion fruit, cut grass and capsicum; high acid; light body; no oak.

white.oak: Usually unoaked (stainless steel, cool fermentation to keep thiols and pyrazines); exceptions are Pessac-Léognan, Pouilly-Fumé cuvées such as Dagueneau, Fumé Blanc in California.
white.markers: Pronounced aroma; very high acid; light to medium body; green (pyrazine: grass, asparagus, capsicum) and tropical (thiol: passion fruit, grapefruit, boxwood) notes; no oak.

classic_regions.name: Sancerre
classic_regions.markers: Restrained, mineral, citrus and green fruit with high acid; flinty silex (Chavignol is Kimmeridgian marl, Bué and Ménétréol caillottes and silex); 12.5 to 13% abv.

classic_regions.name: Pouilly-Fumé
classic_regions.markers: Across the river: smoky, flinty (silex) and slightly fuller than Sancerre.

classic_regions.name: Menetou-Salon
classic_regions.markers: Softer, fruitier Sancerre neighbour.

classic_regions.name: Marlborough
classic_regions.markers: Pungent and pronounced: passion fruit, grapefruit, gooseberry, cut grass and capsicum, high acid, often 2 to 6 g/l sugar; Wairau and Awatere valleys.

classic_regions.name: Elgin
classic_regions.markers: Cool Cape: green fig, citrus and flint, between Loire and Marlborough in style.

classic_regions.name: Valle de Casablanca
classic_regions.markers: Cool, foggy Casablanca and Leyda: citrus, herbaceous and saline.

classic_regions.name: Adelaide Hills
classic_regions.markers: Lime, passion fruit and cut grass, slightly riper and softer than Marlborough.

classic_regions.name: Südsteiermark
classic_regions.markers: Styrian Sauvignon: elderflower, blackcurrant leaf and smoky minerality, often with large-oak ageing for Rieden wines.

sweet.oak: Blended with Sémillon in barrique for Sauternes.

classic_regions.name: Sauternes
classic_regions.markers: A minor partner (10 to 20%) giving acid and aroma in Sauternes.

confused_with.tell: Grüner has white pepper, lentil and green bean, more body and less pungent aroma.
Unoaked Hunter Semillon is lower in alcohol, lighter, and less aromatic, with lemon and lanolin.
Verdejo has fennel, bitter almond and a slight bitter finish.

semillon.name: Sémillon
semillon.markers: Lemon, grass and lanolin; waxy texture; toast and honey with age; the backbone of Sauternes.

white.label: Unoaked, early-picked (Hunter Valley style)
white.oak: Unoaked in the Hunter Valley; bottle age gives toast and honey without oak.
white.markers: Low alcohol, light body, high acid, neutral when young; toast and honey with bottle age.

classic_regions.name: Hunter Valley
classic_regions.markers: Picked early at 10 to 11.5% abv: light, lemon and grass, high acid; after 5 to 10 years in bottle develops toast, honey and lanolin without oak.

white_oaked.label: Oaked blend (Pessac-Léognan style)
white_oaked.oak: Barrel-fermented and aged on lees in Pessac-Léognan blends with Sauvignon.

classic_regions.name: Pessac-Léognan
classic_regions.markers: Blended white Graves (Haut-Brion, Domaine de Chevalier, Smith Haut Lafitte): citrus, wax and toasty oak, structured and long-lived.

classic_regions.name: Margaret River
classic_regions.markers: SBS blends (Sémillon-Sauvignon), crisp and grassy.

botrytis.oak: Sauternes ages 18 to 36 months in barrique, often a high share new.
botrytis.markers: Luscious; marmalade, apricot and saffron; oily texture; high alcohol for a sweet wine.

classic_regions.name: Sauternes
classic_regions.markers: Botrytised Sémillon (about 80%) with Sauvignon: apricot, marmalade, saffron and honey, oily texture, 13 to 14% abv, 100 to 150 g/l sugar, medium+ acid.

classic_regions.name: Barsac
classic_regions.markers: Barsac is often lighter, fresher and more citrus-driven than Sauternes, on limestone.

classic_regions.name: Riverina
classic_regions.markers: De Bortoli Noble One (1982 onwards): Australian botrytised Sémillon.

confused_with.tell: Sauvignon is more aromatic and pungent.
Chardonnay has more body and fruit; Semillon is waxier and lighter in Hunter style.

muscadelle.name: Muscadelle
muscadelle.markers: Floral, grapey; in Rutherglen fortified Topaque with tea leaves and toffee.

sweet.oak: Aged in old casks under hot tin roofs for years.

classic_regions.name: Rutherglen
classic_regions.markers: Rutherglen Topaque (formerly Tokay): fortified Muscadelle with cold tea, toffee and malt; Rutherglen, Classic, Grand and Rare levels.

sweet.note: In Rutherglen Topaque is fortified; this style sits here as a sweet, oxidative wine.

classic_regions.name: Bordeaux
classic_regions.markers: A floral minority partner in Bordeaux whites and Sauternes.

tannat.name: Tannat
tannat.markers: Very high tannin, deep colour, dark fruit and high acid.

red.oak: Often barrique-aged; micro-oxygenation was invented in Madiran (Patrick Ducournau, 1990) to tame its tannin.
red.markers: Highest tannin among common red grapes (rich in procyanidins); deep colour; high acid.

classic_regions.name: Madiran
classic_regions.markers: Very high tannin, dark fruit, firm, needs years; Montus and Bouscassé.

classic_regions.name: Canelones
classic_regions.markers: Uruguay's national grape: riper, rounder tannin, plum and raspberry, sometimes blended with Merlot or Pinot Noir.

petit-manseng.name: Petit Manseng
petit-manseng.markers: Pineapple and spice with very high acid.

sweet.markers: Very high acid even at high sugar; tropical fruit and spice.

classic_regions.name: Jurançon
classic_regions.markers: Passerillé (raisined on the vine): pineapple, mango and spice with searing acid, 50 to 120 g/l sugar balanced by high acid.

classic_regions.name: Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh
classic_regions.markers: Late-harvest sweet whites from the Madiran zone.

classic_regions.name: Virginia
classic_regions.markers: Dry to off-dry, tropical and high acid.

classic_regions.name: Jurançon
classic_regions.markers: Jurançon sec, blended with Gros Manseng.

white.markers: High acid, tropical-citrus aroma.

classic_regions.name: Jurançon
classic_regions.markers: Jurançon sec: citrus, quince and pineapple with high acid.

classic_regions.name: Gascony and the Pyrenees
classic_regions.markers: Crisp, fruity, often off-dry Gascony whites with Colombard and Ugni Blanc.

colombard.name: Colombard
colombard.markers: Light, crisp, grapefruit and passion fruit.

white.markers: High acid, light, tropical-citrus aroma.

classic_regions.name: Western Cape
classic_regions.markers: Bulk and brandy base in the Breede River and Olifants River, plus crisp varietal wines.

classic_regions.name: Gascony and the Pyrenees
classic_regions.markers: Crisp, tropical Côtes de Gascogne IGP whites.

ugni-blanc.name: Ugni Blanc
ugni-blanc.markers: Neutral, high acid; Cognac base; Trebbiano Toscano in Italy.

white.oak: Rarely oaked as a table wine.
white.markers: Neutral, high acid, light; mostly distilled (Cognac) as Ugni Blanc, or Trebbiano Toscano in central Italy.

classic_regions.name: Trebbiano d'Abruzzo
classic_regions.markers: Trebbiano d'Abruzzo is a different variety (Trebbiano Abruzzese), richer when well made.

classic_regions.name: Gascony and the Pyrenees
classic_regions.markers: Crisp base wine; also the main Cognac and Armagnac grape.

sweet.oak: Vin Santo ages several years in small caratelli under the roof.

classic_regions.name: Vin Santo del Chianti Classico
classic_regions.markers: Tuscan Vin Santo from dried Trebbiano and Malvasia: nutty, oxidative, caramel and dried apricot.

folle-blanche.name: Folle Blanche
folle-blanche.markers: Very high acid, neutral; Gros Plant and Armagnac.

white.markers: Very high acid, light body, neutral.

classic_regions.name: Gros Plant du Pays Nantais
classic_regions.markers: Gros Plant du Pays Nantais: very tart, light, low alcohol, with oysters.

red.markers: Red fruit with a green, peppery and ferrous edge.

classic_regions.name: Marcillac
classic_regions.markers: Marcillac (min 90% Fer Servadou, called Mansois): peppery, redcurrant and iron, on red ferruginous soils.

red.markers: Violet and liquorice, soft tannin, low acid.

classic_regions.name: Fronton
classic_regions.markers: Fronton: violet and liquorice, soft and fruity, best young; also rosé.

mauzac.name: Mauzac
mauzac.markers: Apple peel and pear; Limoux and Gaillac sparkling.

sparkling.markers: Apple skin, green and bruised apple; ancestral-method fizz.

classic_regions.name: Limoux
classic_regions.markers: Blanquette de Limoux (min 90% Mauzac) and Blanquette Méthode Ancestrale (100% Mauzac, single fermentation finished in bottle, 7% abv region): green and dried apple skin.

classic_regions.name: Gaillac
classic_regions.markers: Gaillac Méthode Ancestrale and perlé whites.

prunelard.name: Prunelard
prunelard.markers: Dark fruit and pepper; rare Gaillac revival.

classic_regions.name: Gaillac
classic_regions.markers: Revived old Gaillac variety, peppery dark fruit.

marselan.name: Marselan
marselan.markers: Cabernet x Grenache: deep colour, supple tannin.

red.markers: Cabernet Sauvignon x Grenache (1961): deep colour, fine tannin, red and black fruit.

classic_regions.name: Ningxia
classic_regions.markers: Rising Chinese speciality, deep colour, soft tannin.

white.markers: Light, low alcohol, very high acid, often slight spritz.

classic_regions.name: Getariako Txakolina
classic_regions.markers: Txakoli: spritzy (retained CO2), 9.5 to 11.5% abv, tart lime and green apple, poured from height.

hondarrabi-beltza.name: Hondarrabi Beltza
hondarrabi-beltza.markers: Tart red Txakoli grape, related to Cabernet Franc.

classic_regions.name: Getariako Txakolina
classic_regions.markers: Rosé (Rosado) Txakoli and light reds.

pinot-noir.name: Pinot Noir
pinot-noir.markers: Translucent pale ruby, high acid, low tannin, red cherry and raspberry, mushroom and forest floor with age.

red.oak: Burgundy: 12 to 20 months in 228 l pièces, 0 to 100% new by appellation and grower; whole-bunch fermentation (stems) adds spice, firmer tannin and a herbal lift.
red.markers: Pale to medium ruby, translucent; high acid; low to medium tannin; red fruit, earth, mushroom and forest floor with age; often whole-bunch spice.

classic_regions.name: Gevrey-Chambertin
classic_regions.markers: Côte de Nuits power: darker cherry, more tannin and structure, earthy and gamey with age.

classic_regions.name: Chambolle-Musigny
classic_regions.markers: The most perfumed and silky village: violets, raspberry and red cherry, lacy tannin on limestone-rich soils.

classic_regions.name: Vosne-Romanée
classic_regions.markers: Spice, silk and depth; home of Romanée-Conti, La Tâche and Richebourg.

classic_regions.name: Pommard
classic_regions.markers: Côte de Beaune but sturdy: dense, firmer tannin, more rustic and earthy.

classic_regions.name: Volnay
classic_regions.markers: Delicate and fragrant: red fruit and flowers, fine tannin, the Chambolle of the Côte de Beaune.

classic_regions.name: Santenay
classic_regions.markers: Firm, earthy village reds at the south of the Côte de Beaune.

classic_regions.name: Mercurey
classic_regions.markers: Côte Chalonnaise: lighter, firmer, earthy.

classic_regions.name: Sancerre
classic_regions.markers: Light Loire Pinot (Sancerre rouge): pale, red-fruited and high in acid.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Alsace Pinot Noir: light to medium, cherry; increasingly serious grand cru-level wines.

classic_regions.name: Russian River Valley
classic_regions.markers: Ripe black cherry and cola, baking spice, 14 to 14.5% abv, generous oak; fog-cooled.

classic_regions.name: Sonoma Coast
classic_regions.markers: Cooler and more structured, brighter acid, savoury.

classic_regions.name: Sta. Rita Hills
classic_regions.markers: Santa Barbara transverse range: bright acid, dark cherry, spice and stem.

classic_regions.name: Dundee Hills
classic_regions.markers: Willamette: red cherry, cranberry, earthy and forest-floor on red Jory volcanic soil; acid between Burgundy and California.

classic_regions.name: Central Otago
classic_regions.markers: Continental extreme: deep for Pinot, ripe black cherry and plum, wild thyme, 13.5 to 14.5% abv, fresh acid.

classic_regions.name: Martinborough
classic_regions.markers: Savoury, structured, darker and more tannic than most NZ Pinot.

classic_regions.name: Yarra Valley
classic_regions.markers: Elegant, red-fruited, medium-bodied; often whole bunch.

classic_regions.name: Mornington Peninsula
classic_regions.markers: Maritime, fine and red-fruited.

classic_regions.name: Baden
classic_regions.markers: Spätburgunder: Kaiserstuhl volcanic and Baden limestone, Burgundian in style.

classic_regions.name: Ahr
classic_regions.markers: Steep slate: red fruit, smoky mineral, fresh and fine.

classic_regions.name: Hemel-en-Aarde Valley
classic_regions.markers: Cape Pinot on shale and clay near the Atlantic: firm, savoury, red-fruited.

classic_regions.name: Valle de Casablanca
classic_regions.markers: Cool coastal Chile: bright, red-fruited, herbal.

sparkling.oak: Mostly tank, some houses ferment in old oak (Krug, Bollinger).
sparkling.markers: Adds body, red fruit and structure to blends.

classic_regions.name: Montagne de Reims
classic_regions.markers: Pinot Noir heartland of Champagne: body, red fruit and structure (Verzenay, Ambonnay, Bouzy).

classic_regions.name: Champagne
classic_regions.markers: Blanc de noirs and the backbone of most blends.

classic_regions.name: Rosé des Riceys
classic_regions.markers: Rosé des Riceys: rare still rosé of Pinot Noir from the Aube.

classic_regions.name: Sancerre
classic_regions.markers: Pale Sancerre rosé.

confused_with.tell: Gamay is purpler with banana or bubblegum carbonic notes, less forest floor and lighter structure.
Grenache is riper with higher alcohol, lower acid, kirsch and garrigue.
Nebbiolo shares the pale colour but has very high tannin, tar and roses and orange rim early.

chardonnay.name: Chardonnay
chardonnay.markers: A chameleon: high acid and citrus when cool (Chablis); butter, toast and stone fruit when oaked and warm. No marked aromatic profile of its own.

white.label: Unoaked cool climate (Chablis style)
white.oak: Chablis is often unoaked (stainless or old oak); many premier and grand crus see some barrel.
white.markers: High acid, light to medium body, citrus and green apple, chalky and saline, little or no oak.

classic_regions.name: Chablis
classic_regions.markers: Steely, high-acid, green apple, lemon and wet stone with a saline, oyster-shell edge on Kimmeridgian marl; 12 to 13% abv.

classic_regions.name: Chablis Grand Cru
classic_regions.markers: Riper, broader and long-lived; seven climats on one southwest-facing slope; honey, smoke and iodine with age.

classic_regions.name: Petit Chablis
classic_regions.markers: Lighter, on Portlandian limestone.

white_oaked.label: Barrel-fermented (Côte de Beaune and New World)
white_oaked.oak: Barrel fermentation and 10 to 18 months in 228 l Burgundian pièces with bâtonnage; MLF usually complete; new oak 0 to 100%.
white_oaked.markers: Medium+ to full body; medium to medium+ acid; stone and tropical fruit; butter (MLF), vanilla, toast and nuts from oak; struck-match reduction in modern styles.

classic_regions.name: Meursault
classic_regions.markers: Rich, nutty, buttery and broad; hazelnut and toast; no grand crus but famous premiers (Perrières, Genevrières, Charmes).

classic_regions.name: Puligny-Montrachet
classic_regions.markers: Tighter, more mineral and floral than Meursault; citrus, white flowers and steely length.

classic_regions.name: Chassagne-Montrachet
classic_regions.markers: Broader and riper than Puligny, often with a hint of nuts.

classic_regions.name: Montrachet
classic_regions.markers: The greatest white Burgundy grand cru: immense concentration, length and longevity.

classic_regions.name: Corton-Charlemagne
classic_regions.markers: Grand cru on marl and limestone: powerful and mineral, slow to open.

classic_regions.name: Pouilly-Fuissé
classic_regions.markers: Mâconnais: riper yellow fruit, generous; premiers crus since 2020.

classic_regions.name: Mâcon Villages
classic_regions.markers: Unoaked or lightly oaked, fruity Mâconnais.

classic_regions.name: Russian River Valley
classic_regions.markers: Ripe tropical and stone fruit, butter, vanilla and toast; 14% abv; full body.

classic_regions.name: Sonoma Coast
classic_regions.markers: Leaner, more mineral modern Californian style.

classic_regions.name: Napa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Carneros-cooled: ripe, rich, buttery and oaky in the classic style.

classic_regions.name: Margaret River
classic_regions.markers: Leeuwin and Pierro: grapefruit, white peach, cashew and struck match; tight, long.

classic_regions.name: Yarra Valley
classic_regions.markers: Modern Australian: early picked, lean, grapefruit, flint (struck-match reduction).

classic_regions.name: Adelaide Hills
classic_regions.markers: Fine, citrus and stone fruit, restrained oak.

classic_regions.name: Hawke's Bay
classic_regions.markers: Rich, stone fruit and oak, with fresh acid.

classic_regions.name: Walker Bay
classic_regions.markers: Hemel-en-Aarde: citrus, mineral, fine oak, Burgundian.

classic_regions.name: Valle del Limarí
classic_regions.markers: Limestone-influenced coastal Chilean Chardonnay: saline, citrus, tense.

sparkling.oak: Mostly stainless steel; some houses ferment in oak.
sparkling.markers: High acid, citrus and chalk; autolytic brioche and toast with lees time.

classic_regions.name: Côte des Blancs
classic_regions.markers: Blanc de blancs from chalk: lemon, citrus and chalky mineral, high acid, finesse (Avize, Cramant, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Oger).

classic_regions.name: Champagne
classic_regions.markers: With Pinot Noir and Meunier, one of the three main Champagne grapes; brings finesse, citrus and ageing potential.

classic_regions.name: Crémant de Bourgogne
classic_regions.markers: Crémant de Bourgogne: traditional method, minimum 9 months on lees.

classic_regions.name: English Wine
classic_regions.markers: English sparkling: very high acid, green apple and lemon, chalk of the Sussex Downs.

classic_regions.name: Franciacorta
classic_regions.markers: Franciacorta: riper, rounder Italian traditional method, 18 months on lees minimum.

classic_regions.name: Tasmania
classic_regions.markers: Tasmanian sparkling: crisp, citrus, fine.

classic_regions.name: Neusiedlersee
classic_regions.markers: Burgenland botrytised Chardonnay blends (Kracher).

confused_with.tell: Chenin has higher acid, quince, honey and lanolin/wet wool, and often some sweetness.
Viognier is perfumed (apricot, honeysuckle), lower acid, oily.
Oaked Sémillon blends are waxier with grassy Sauvignon lift.
Marsanne is lower acid, oilier, with marzipan and pear.

gamay.name: Gamay
gamay.markers: Pale purple, high acid, low tannin, bright red fruit, banana and bubblegum from carbonic maceration.

red.oak: Mostly vat-aged; cru wines may see old foudres or some barrique.
red.markers: Pale to medium purple, high acid, low tannin, very fruity (red cherry, raspberry), carbonic maceration notes (banana, bubblegum, kirsch) in lighter styles.

classic_regions.name: Beaujolais
classic_regions.markers: Light, juicy, pale purple, carbonic banana and bubblegum; Beaujolais Nouveau released third Thursday of November.

classic_regions.name: Fleurie
classic_regions.markers: Fragrant, floral (iris, violet), silky; pink granite.

classic_regions.name: Morgon
classic_regions.markers: Firmer, darker; Côte du Py (blue schist and volcanic rock) wines take on cherry and a Burgundian earthiness with age ("morgonner").

classic_regions.name: Moulin-à-Vent
classic_regions.markers: The most structured cru, manganese-rich granite; ages like Burgundy.

classic_regions.name: Brouilly
classic_regions.markers: The largest cru, fruity and supple.

classic_regions.name: Côte de Brouilly
classic_regions.markers: Volcanic diorite (blue stone) of Mont Brouilly: more mineral, firmer.

classic_regions.name: Chiroubles
classic_regions.markers: High (up to 400 m+) granite: the lightest, most delicate cru.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Amour
classic_regions.markers: The northernmost cru, soft and fruity.

classic_regions.name: Juliénas
classic_regions.markers: Firm, spicy, darker fruit.

classic_regions.name: Chénas
classic_regions.markers: The smallest cru; sturdy, woodsy.

classic_regions.name: Régnié
classic_regions.markers: The newest cru (1988), supple and fruity.

classic_regions.name: Valais
classic_regions.markers: Dôle is a Pinot Noir and Gamay blend from the Valais.

classic_regions.name: Côte roannaise
classic_regions.markers: Loire Gamay on granite.

classic_regions.name: Touraine
classic_regions.markers: Touraine Gamay rosé and reds.

confused_with.tell: Pinot has more complexity, forest floor and finer tannin; less purple.

aligote.name: Aligoté
aligote.markers: Tart lemon and green apple, light.

white.markers: Very high acid, light, lemon and apple.

classic_regions.name: Bouzeron
classic_regions.markers: Bouzeron: the only village appellation for Aligoté (since 1997); fuller, more mineral.

classic_regions.name: Bourgogne aligoté
classic_regions.markers: Very tart; the base for Kir.

melon-de-bourgogne.name: Melon de Bourgogne
melon-de-bourgogne.markers: Neutral, saline, tart, yeasty sur lie; light alcohol.

white.oak: Unoaked; aged sur lie in tank.
white.markers: Neutral, light, high acid, saline; lees give bread and slight creaminess and a faint spritz.

classic_regions.name: Muscadet Sèvre et Maine
classic_regions.markers: Muscadet sur lie (kept on its fine lees over winter and bottled straight off them): saline, lemon, yeasty, faint spritz; max 12% abv.

classic_regions.name: Clisson
classic_regions.markers: Cru communal Clisson: granite, long lees ageing (24 months minimum), riper and more complex.

classic_regions.name: Gorges
classic_regions.markers: Gorges: gabbro and quartz; firm and mineral.

classic_regions.name: Le Pallet
classic_regions.markers: Le Pallet: gneiss and gabbro.

chenin-blanc.name: Chenin Blanc
chenin-blanc.markers: High acid, apple and quince, wet wool and lanolin, honey with age; any sweetness level.

white.label: Dry (sec)
white.oak: Ranges from tank to old foudres and demi-muids; some new oak in Savennières and South Africa.
white.markers: High acid even when ripe; apple and quince; wet wool and lanolin; honey and beeswax with age.

classic_regions.name: Savennières
classic_regions.markers: Bone-dry, austere, wax, quince and wet wool; needs 5 to 10 years; schist; Coulée de Serrant monopole.

classic_regions.name: Vouvray
classic_regions.markers: Vouvray sec: apple, quince, chalk and honey with searing acid on tuffeau and silex.

classic_regions.name: Saumur
classic_regions.markers: Saumur blanc, chalky, increasingly fine and dry (Brézé hill).

classic_regions.name: Swartland
classic_regions.markers: Old bush-vine Swartland: riper, rounder, stone fruit and honey, oaked; 13 to 14% abv.

classic_regions.name: Stellenbosch
classic_regions.markers: Cape Chenin: tropical, ripe apple, honey, sometimes oaked.

off_dry.label: Demi-sec and tendre
off_dry.markers: Sweetness balanced by searing acid; quince, honey.

classic_regions.name: Vouvray
classic_regions.markers: Demi-sec and tendre Vouvray in warm years, high acid balances the sugar.

classic_regions.name: Montlouis-sur-Loire
classic_regions.markers: Montlouis-sur-Loire, opposite Vouvray across the Loire, similar range.

botrytis.markers: Sweet but high acid; quince, honey, marmalade; long-lived.

classic_regions.name: Quarts de Chaume
classic_regions.markers: Quarts de Chaume (Grand Cru, 2011): Layon botrytis or passerillage, min 298 g/l must sugar; long-lived.

classic_regions.name: Bonnezeaux
classic_regions.markers: Bonnezeaux: rich, schist, botrytis.

classic_regions.name: Coteaux du Layon
classic_regions.markers: Coteaux du Layon: sweet, more variable.

classic_regions.name: Vouvray
classic_regions.markers: Moelleux in great years.

classic_regions.name: Crémant de Loire
classic_regions.markers: Crémant de Loire: traditional method, Chenin-led with Chardonnay and Cabernet Franc.

classic_regions.name: Vouvray
classic_regions.markers: Vouvray pétillant and mousseux.

confused_with.tell: Chardonnay lacks the quince, lanolin and searing acid; usually more oak and butter.
Riesling is more aromatic (lime, petrol, floral), lighter, and lacks the waxy, wool texture.
Hunter Semillon is lighter and lower in alcohol, lemon and grass.

romorantin.name: Romorantin
romorantin.markers: High acid, waxy, citrus; Cour-Cheverny only.

classic_regions.name: Cour-Cheverny
classic_regions.markers: Cour-Cheverny: the only appellation for Romorantin; high acid, wax and honey.

red.markers: Pale, light, peppery (rotundone) red.

classic_regions.name: Coteaux du Loir
classic_regions.markers: Coteaux du Loir: pale, peppery, light; also rosé.

classic_regions.name: Rosé d'Anjou
classic_regions.markers: Rosé d'Anjou: off-dry, light, Grolleau-based.

auxerrois.name: Auxerrois
auxerrois.markers: Soft, low acid, melon and pear; part of Alsace Pinot Blanc.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Blended into Alsace Pinot Blanc (both may be labelled Pinot Blanc), soft and low in acid.

classic_regions.name: Moselle Luxembourgeoise
classic_regions.markers: Luxembourg: soft, round.

pinot-blanc.name: Pinot Blanc
pinot-blanc.markers: Neutral, apple and pear, almond, medium acid, round.

white.oak: Mostly unoaked; Weissburgunder in Germany and Austria may see oak.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Alsace Pinot Blanc: soft, round, apple and almond.

classic_regions.name: Pfalz
classic_regions.markers: Weissburgunder: fresh and fruity, top GGs fuller.

classic_regions.name: Alto Adige
classic_regions.markers: Pinot Bianco: crisp, mineral, ageworthy from Terlano.

classic_regions.name: Leithaberg
classic_regions.markers: Leithaberg DAC white (Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger, Grüner): limestone and schist.

classic_regions.name: Crémant d'Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Crémant d'Alsace base.

pinot-gris.name: Pinot Gris
pinot-gris.markers: Grape with pink-grey skins: neutral and crisp as Grigio; pear, honey, smoke and spice, full and low-acid as Alsace Gris.

white.label: Light, crisp (Italian Pinot Grigio style)
white.markers: Neutral, light, crisp; early picked.

classic_regions.name: delle Venezie
classic_regions.markers: Pinot Grigio delle Venezie: neutral, light, crisp.

classic_regions.name: Alto Adige
classic_regions.markers: Alto Adige and Friuli Pinot Grigio: more concentration, still crisp.

white_rich.label: Rich, oily (Alsace style)
white_rich.oak: Large old foudres in Alsace; some barrel in Oregon.
white_rich.markers: Full body, low to medium acid, pear, honey, spice and smoke, often a touch of sweetness.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Alsace Pinot Gris: full, oily, spicy, smoky, often some residual sugar; up to 14% abv; vendanges tardives and SGN possible.

classic_regions.name: Willamette Valley
classic_regions.markers: Oregon Pinot Gris: medium-bodied, pear and spice, between Italy and Alsace.

classic_regions.name: Marlborough
classic_regions.markers: NZ Pinot Gris: off-dry, pear and spice.

classic_regions.name: Friuli Colli Orientali
classic_regions.markers: Ramato: copper-coloured skin-contact Pinot Grigio, a Friulian tradition.

confused_with.tell: Gewürz is far more aromatic (lychee, rose).
Viognier is more floral and apricot.

gewurztraminer.name: Gewürztraminer
gewurztraminer.markers: Lychee, rose and ginger; low acid; full, oily body; high alcohol; deeper colour.

white.markers: Deep colour for a young white (pink-skinned grape); pronounced lychee, rose, Turkish delight; low acid; high alcohol; oily; bitter phenolic finish.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Alsace: pronounced lychee and rose, oily, full, 13.5 to 14.5% abv, often off-dry; vendanges tardives and SGN in warm grand crus.

classic_regions.name: Alsace grand cru Hengst
classic_regions.markers: Hengst: calcareous marl, powerful, spicy Gewurztraminer.

classic_regions.name: Alsace grand cru Furstentum
classic_regions.markers: Furstentum: warm amphitheatre, rich Gewurztraminer.

classic_regions.name: Alto Adige
classic_regions.markers: Traminer Aromatico from Tramin (Termeno), the village the name may come from: drier, fresher.

classic_regions.name: Pfalz
classic_regions.markers: Pfalz Gewürztraminer: lush, often sweet.

white.note: Cis-rose oxide is a key rose and lychee odorant shared with lychee fruit.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Sélection de grains nobles.

confused_with.tell: Muscat smells of fresh grapes and orange blossom, lighter body, higher acid.
Viognier has apricot and peach, less lychee and spice.
Torrontés is lighter, higher in acid, with a bitter grapy finish.

riesling.name: Riesling
riesling.markers: Very high acid, aromatic (lime, green apple, peach, flowers), never oaky, from bone dry to luscious; petrol with age.

white.label: Light, off-dry to medium-sweet (Mosel Kabinett style)
white.oak: No new oak; tank or old Fuder (1,000 l).
white.markers: Pronounced aroma, very high acid, low alcohol, light body; residual sugar balanced by acid.

classic_regions.name: Mosel
classic_regions.markers: Mosel Kabinett: 7.5 to 9% abv, off-dry to medium-sweet, green apple, white peach, flowers and slate, piercing acid.

classic_regions.name: Saar
classic_regions.markers: Saar: even more steely and racy.

classic_regions.name: Wehlener Sonnenuhr
classic_regions.markers: Middle Mosel benchmark Einzellage on blue Devonian slate.

classic_regions.name: Scharzhofberg
classic_regions.markers: Saar benchmark (Egon Müller).

white_dry.label: Dry (Trocken, Clare Valley, Alsace, Wachau)
white_dry.oak: No new oak; large old casks or stainless steel.
white_dry.markers: High acid, citrus and stone fruit, floral; petrol (TDN) and toast develop with bottle age; never noticeably oaked.

classic_regions.name: Clare Valley
classic_regions.markers: Bone dry, lime juice and lime blossom, high acid, 11.5 to 12.5% abv, toast and kerosene within 5 to 8 years; screwcap since 2000.

classic_regions.name: Eden Valley
classic_regions.markers: Floral, lime, slightly more delicate than Clare.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Dry, fuller (12.5 to 13.5% abv), stone fruit, mineral and spicy; grand crus such as Schlossberg, Rangen, Brand.

classic_regions.name: Wachau
classic_regions.markers: Smaragd (min 12.5% abv, under Vinea Wachau rules): ripe apricot, peach, rich and dry with high acid; Federspiel lighter.

classic_regions.name: Kamptal
classic_regions.markers: Heiligenstein: powerful, mineral Riesling from Permian sandstone.

classic_regions.name: Rheingau
classic_regions.markers: Rheingau: firmer, fuller, more structured; the Charta and the Grosses Gewächs movement.

classic_regions.name: Pfalz
classic_regions.markers: Pfalz Grosses Gewächs: ripe, dry, powerful (Forst, Deidesheim).

classic_regions.name: Nahe
classic_regions.markers: Nahe: mineral, varied volcanic and slate soils.

classic_regions.name: Waipara Valley
classic_regions.markers: Waipara and Central Otago: off-dry to dry, citrus.

classic_regions.name: Finger Lakes
classic_regions.markers: New York Finger Lakes: high acid, dry to off-dry, slate and lime.

classic_regions.name: Columbia Valley
classic_regions.markers: Washington: riper, fruit-forward, off-dry to dry.

white_dry.note: TDN gives petrol; sun exposure raises it (Riesling averages 6.4 ug/l TDN vs 1.3 ug/l for other varietals in a cited study).

classic_regions.name: Mosel
classic_regions.markers: Auslese: 7 to 8% abv, lush but racy.

classic_regions.name: Niagara Peninsula
classic_regions.markers: Icewine: grapes naturally frozen on the vine (min -8 C in Canada).

classic_regions.name: Rheingau
classic_regions.markers: Spätlese was born at Schloss Johannisberg (1775).

classic_regions.name: Mosel
classic_regions.markers: Beerenauslese and Trockenbeerenauslese: 5.5 to 7% abv, extremely sweet, searing acid.

classic_regions.name: Alsace
classic_regions.markers: Sélection de grains nobles.

classic_regions.name: Neusiedlersee
classic_regions.markers: Burgenland TBA.

classic_regions.name: Mosel
classic_regions.markers: Riesling Sekt (b.A.).

confused_with.tell: Chenin is waxier, with quince and wet wool.
Albariño is saline, lower acid, more peachy, no petrol.
Grüner is peppery and less aromatic.
Furmint has smoky quince and pear, more body, no petrol.

white.markers: Neutral, earthy and herbal with savoury minerality.

classic_regions.name: Franken
classic_regions.markers: Franken Silvaner in the flat Bocksbeutel: earthy, mineral, savoury on Muschelkalk (shell limestone); Würzburger Stein.

classic_regions.name: Rheinhessen
classic_regions.markers: Rheinhessen Silvaner: the largest plantings.

classic_regions.name: Alsace grand cru Zotzenberg
classic_regions.markers: Zotzenberg: the only Alsace grand cru allowed Sylvaner (since 2006).

savagnin.name: Savagnin
savagnin.markers: High acid; vin jaune walnut and curry spice from voile; Château-Chalon.

oxidative.label: Vin jaune (under voile)
oxidative.oak: At least 60 months in barrel under a film of yeast (voile) without topping up, not released before December of the sixth year after harvest; bottled in the 62 cl clavelin.
oxidative.markers: Flor-aged but unfortified: walnut, curry spice, green apple, high acid, medium+ alcohol (13.5 to 15%); not sweet.

classic_regions.name: Château-Chalon
classic_regions.markers: Château-Chalon: vin jaune only, grey marl, the most intense; curry spice, walnut and green apple.

classic_regions.name: Arbois
classic_regions.markers: Arbois vin jaune and sous voile whites.

classic_regions.name: Côtes du Jura
classic_regions.markers: Côtes du Jura vin jaune.

classic_regions.name: Arbois
classic_regions.markers: Ouillé Savagnin: fresh, citrus, saline.

confused_with.tell: Fino Sherry is fortified (15%), lighter, lower acid, with bread and chamomile.

trousseau.name: Trousseau
trousseau.markers: Pale, red fruit and pepper, Jura red.

classic_regions.name: Arbois
classic_regions.markers: Arbois (Pupillin): pale, red fruit, spicy; darker than Poulsard.

classic_regions.name: Dão
classic_regions.markers: Known as Bastardo in Portugal.

red.markers: Very pale (thin skins), light, red fruit.

classic_regions.name: Arbois
classic_regions.markers: Arbois Ploussard (Pupillin): almost rosé-pale, delicate, earthy red fruit.

chasselas.name: Chasselas
chasselas.markers: Neutral, soft, low acid; Swiss Fendant and Dézaley.

white.oak: Large old wood or tank; often full MLF in Vaud.
white.markers: Neutral, low acid, light; lees and MLF give roundness; mineral and smoky with age.

classic_regions.name: Dézaley
classic_regions.markers: Lavaux grand cru: richer, mineral, toasty and long-lived on steep lake terraces.

classic_regions.name: Lavaux
classic_regions.markers: Lavaux UNESCO terraces over Lake Geneva.

classic_regions.name: Valais
classic_regions.markers: Fendant (Valais name): fuller, smoky.

classic_regions.name: Crépy
classic_regions.markers: Haute-Savoie Chasselas.

classic_regions.name: Apremont
classic_regions.markers: Apremont: light, floral, alpine.

classic_regions.name: Abymes
classic_regions.markers: Abymes: crisp, low alcohol.

mondeuse-noire.name: Mondeuse Noire
mondeuse-noire.markers: Purple, peppery, violet, high acid; Savoie.

classic_regions.name: Arbin
classic_regions.markers: Arbin: Mondeuse on scree, peppery and violet.

sparkling.markers: Fruity, round, matures quickly in blends.

classic_regions.name: Vallée de la Marne
classic_regions.markers: Vallée de la Marne: frost-resistant, fruity, gives early-maturing roundness; growers now bottle 100% Meunier.

classic_regions.name: Champagne
classic_regions.markers: One of the three main Champagne grapes.

classic_regions.name: Württemberg
classic_regions.markers: Schwarzriesling in Württemberg.

fruhburgunder.name: Frühburgunder
fruhburgunder.markers: Early-ripening Pinot Noir mutation: softer, darker.

classic_regions.name: Ahr
classic_regions.markers: Ahr Frühburgunder: early-ripening Pinot mutation, darker, softer acid than Spätburgunder.

classic_regions.name: Franken
classic_regions.markers: Bürgstadt (Franken), on red sandstone.

syrah.name: Syrah
syrah.markers: Deep purple; black fruit, black pepper, violet, olive and smoked meat (cool) or blackberry, chocolate and liquorice (warm); firm tannin.

red.label: Cool and moderate climate (Northern Rhône style)
red.oak: Northern Rhône: demi-muids (600 l) and barriques, little to moderate new oak; some whole-bunch fermentation.
red.markers: Deep purple; black fruit; black pepper (rotundone), violet, olive, smoked meat and bacon fat; medium+ acid; medium+ tannin; leather and game with age.

classic_regions.name: Côte Rôtie
classic_regions.markers: The most perfumed: violet, raspberry and black olive, finer tannin; up to 20% Viognier co-fermented; Côte Brune (schist, iron-rich) firmer, Côte Blonde (granite, gneiss) softer.

classic_regions.name: Hermitage
classic_regions.markers: Granite hill above Tain: the most powerful and long-lived, dense black fruit, meaty, high tannin; Bessards (granite) for structure, Méal (limestone pebbles) for richness.

classic_regions.name: Cornas
classic_regions.markers: 100% Syrah, granite amphitheatre: rustic, sauvage, black fruit and smoke, firm tannin.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Joseph
classic_regions.markers: Lighter, red and black fruit with pepper on granite, a long narrow appellation on the west bank.

classic_regions.name: Crozes-Hermitage
classic_regions.markers: Larger, flatter, fruitier and earlier-drinking; the Les Chassis plain and northern granite hills.

classic_regions.name: Walla Walla Valley
classic_regions.markers: The Rocks District (Milton-Freewater) basalt cobbles: savoury, funky (olive, umami, iron, smoked meat), ripe fruit.

classic_regions.name: Hawke's Bay
classic_regions.markers: Gimblett Gravels Syrah: white pepper and violet with fresh acid.

classic_regions.name: Grampians
classic_regions.markers: Great Western: peppery, spicy cool-climate Australian Shiraz.

classic_regions.name: Canberra District
classic_regions.markers: Clonakilla: co-fermented with Viognier in the Côte-Rôtie manner.

classic_regions.name: Swartland
classic_regions.markers: Old-vine Swartland on schist and granite: savoury, peppery, restrained.

red_warm.label: Warm climate (Barossa Shiraz style)
red_warm.oak: Barossa and McLaren Vale: often American oak (coconut, vanilla) or new French; 12 to 24 months; Grange uses new American oak.
red_warm.markers: Full body, high alcohol, ripe black fruit and liquorice, chocolate and mocha, mint or eucalyptus, low to medium acid, plush tannin.

classic_regions.name: Barossa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Rich, ripe blackberry and plum, chocolate, mocha and liquorice; 14.5 to 15.5% abv; full body; soft, ripe acid (often adjusted); velvety tannin; Old Vine Charter ancestor vines (125+ years).

classic_regions.name: McLaren Vale
classic_regions.markers: Mediterranean, maritime: ripe, rich, with dark chocolate, savoury herbs and a fresher finish.

classic_regions.name: Hunter Valley
classic_regions.markers: Hunter Shiraz: medium-bodied, earthy, leathery ("sweaty saddle"), lower alcohol.

classic_regions.name: Heathcote
classic_regions.markers: Cambrian red soils: deep, plush, minty, rich fruit.

classic_regions.name: Eden Valley
classic_regions.markers: Higher, cooler: Hill of Grace and Mount Edelstone, spicier and more perfumed.

classic_regions.name: Paso Robles
classic_regions.markers: Warm Central Coast: ripe, rich, high alcohol, Rhône-style blends.

classic_regions.name: San Juan
classic_regions.markers: Warm, fruit-forward Argentine Syrah.

classic_regions.name: Tavel
classic_regions.markers: Part of Tavel and Côtes du Rhône rosé blends.

classic_regions.name: Grampians
classic_regions.markers: Sparkling Shiraz (Great Western): deep red, off-dry, a uniquely Australian style.

confused_with.tell: Grenache is paler, kirsch-scented, lower in tannin and higher in alcohol.
Malbec lacks the pepper and meat, with more violet and plush plum.
Mourvèdre is more gamey, earthy and tannic, with less pepper.
Petite Sirah is even darker, more tannic and less aromatic.

viognier.name: Viognier
viognier.markers: Apricot, peach, honeysuckle; low acid; oily; high alcohol.

white.oak: Condrieu: part barrel fermentation (often older barrels), lees stirring; many New World versions unoaked.
white.markers: Pronounced apricot and floral perfume; low acid; full, oily body; high alcohol; slightly bitter phenolic finish.

classic_regions.name: Condrieu
classic_regions.markers: Condrieu: heady apricot, peach, honeysuckle and violets; full, oily; low acid; 13.5 to 14.5% abv; granite terraces; drink young.

classic_regions.name: Château-Grillet
classic_regions.markers: Château-Grillet: single-estate monopole (3.8 ha), more restrained, long-lived.

classic_regions.name: Eden Valley
classic_regions.markers: Yalumba pioneered Australian Viognier: apricot, ginger, rich.

classic_regions.name: Virginia
classic_regions.markers: Virginia's signature white.

confused_with.tell: Gewürz shows lychee and rose, more spice.
Chardonnay has more acid and less floral perfume.
Marsanne is less aromatic, more pear and marzipan.
Roussanne is more herbal tea and pear, with better acid.

marsanne.name: Marsanne
marsanne.markers: Full, oily, low acid, pear and almond, honey with age.

white.oak: Large old wood or some barrique.
white.markers: Neutral when young, low acid, full and oily; marzipan, pear and honey; ages to nuts and beeswax.

classic_regions.name: Hermitage
classic_regions.markers: White Hermitage (mostly Marsanne with Roussanne): full, oily, pear and almond, honey and nuts after 10+ years, after a dumb phase.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Joseph
classic_regions.markers: Saint-Joseph blanc.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Péray
classic_regions.markers: Saint-Péray: still and sparkling Marsanne and Roussanne.

classic_regions.name: Nagambie Lakes
classic_regions.markers: Tahbilk: old-vine (1927) Marsanne that ages to honeysuckle and toast.

roussanne.name: Roussanne
roussanne.markers: Herbal tea, pear and honey; fuller and more aromatic than Marsanne.

white.markers: Herbal tea and pear, better acid than Marsanne.

classic_regions.name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
classic_regions.markers: Château de Beaucastel Roussanne Vieilles Vignes: herbal tea, pear and honey.

classic_regions.name: Saint-Joseph
classic_regions.markers: Part of northern Rhône whites.

classic_regions.name: Vin de Savoie Chignin-Bergeron
classic_regions.markers: Chignin-Bergeron: Roussanne (Bergeron) in Savoie, fresher.

grenache.name: Grenache
grenache.markers: Pale for its weight; high alcohol, low acid, soft tannin; kirsch, strawberry jam, garrigue and white pepper; garnet early.

red.oak: Often large old foudres or concrete (Rayas, Châteauneuf); some barrique.
red.markers: Pale to medium ruby, quick to garnet; high alcohol; low acid; soft to medium tannin; red fruit, kirsch, garrigue and white pepper; jammy when warm.

classic_regions.name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
classic_regions.markers: Up to 13 permitted grapes, Grenache-led: kirsch, strawberry jam, garrigue, leather; 14.5 to 15.5% abv; full; soft acid; galets roulés on the La Crau plateau, sand at Rayas.

classic_regions.name: Gigondas
classic_regions.markers: Gigondas (min 50% Grenache): firmer, more rustic and higher-altitude, limestone of the Dentelles.

classic_regions.name: Vacqueyras
classic_regions.markers: Vacqueyras: rustic, dark Grenache-Syrah.

classic_regions.name: Côtes du Rhône Villages
classic_regions.markers: Côtes du Rhône Villages: Grenache-led blends.

classic_regions.name: Priorat
classic_regions.markers: Garnacha on llicorella schist: concentrated, mineral, high alcohol, firmer tannin, often with Cariñena and Cabernet.

classic_regions.name: Campo de Borja
classic_regions.markers: Old-vine Garnacha, the "Empire of Garnacha": ripe, rich, good value.

classic_regions.name: Calatayud
classic_regions.markers: Very old bush vines at altitude on slate.

classic_regions.name: Vinos de Madrid
classic_regions.markers: Sierra de Gredos granite Garnacha (Comando G): pale, perfumed, Pinot-like.

classic_regions.name: Cannonau di Sardegna
classic_regions.markers: Cannonau in Sardinia: dry, robust, ripe.

classic_regions.name: McLaren Vale
classic_regions.markers: Old-vine McLaren Vale and Barossa Grenache: bright red fruit, spice, often lighter modern styles.

classic_regions.name: Barossa Valley
classic_regions.markers: GSM blends (Grenache, Shiraz, Mourvèdre).

classic_regions.name: Côtes de Provence
classic_regions.markers: Very pale, dry, delicate: red berry, citrus and herbal; pressed directly.

classic_regions.name: Tavel
classic_regions.markers: Tavel: rosé only; deeper, fuller, more vinous; maceration; Grenache-based.

classic_regions.name: Navarra
classic_regions.markers: Navarra rosado by saignée: deeper colour, fruity.

fortified.oak: Rimage (vintage, early-bottled, fruity) or oxidative ageing in barrels and outdoor bonbonnes (glass demijohns) giving rancio.
fortified.markers: Vin doux naturel: fortified during fermentation, sweet, high alcohol; rancio, coffee and walnut with oxidative ageing.

classic_regions.name: Banyuls
classic_regions.markers: Banyuls VDN (min 50% Grenache Noir): mutage on skins, 15 to 18% abv; rimage (red fruit) or rancio (nuts, coffee) styles; terraced schist.

classic_regions.name: Maury
classic_regions.markers: Maury: Grenache VDN on black schist; also Maury sec reds.

classic_regions.name: Rivesaltes
classic_regions.markers: Rivesaltes ambré and tuilé.

confused_with.tell: Pinot has much higher acid, lower alcohol and forest-floor complexity.
Syrah is deeper, more tannic, black-fruited and peppery.
Tempranillo has more tannin, savoury leather and tobacco, and American oak dill in Rioja.

grenache-blanc.name: Grenache Blanc
grenache-blanc.markers: Full, low acid, high alcohol, herbal; southern Rhône and Catalonia.

white.markers: Full, high alcohol, low acid, green apple and herbs.

classic_regions.name: Châteauneuf-du-Pape
classic_regions.markers: White Châteauneuf: round, high alcohol, fennel and pear.

classic_regions.name: Terra Alta
classic_regions.markers: Terra Alta Garnatxa Blanca: rich, herbal, Catalan benchmark.

classic_regions.name: Côtes du Roussillon
classic_regions.markers: Roussillon whites, often blended.

mourvedre.name: Mourvèdre
mourvedre.markers: Gamey, meaty, earthy, black fruit and garrigue, high tannin.

red.oak: Bandol: minimum 18 months in oak (traditionally large foudres) before release.
red.markers: Deep colour, high tannin, gamey and meaty, black fruit and herbs; reductive when young.

classic_regions.name: Bandol
classic_regions.markers: Bandol rouge (min 50% Mourvèdre): dense, gamey, black fruit, garrigue, firm tannin; long-lived; terraces (restanques) above the sea.

classic_regions.name: Jumilla
classic_regions.markers: Monastrell: ripe, high alcohol, black fruit and liquorice, warm and soft.

classic_regions.name: Yecla
classic_regions.markers: Yecla and Alicante Monastrell; also Fondillón (aged sweet wine).

classic_regions.name: Barossa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Mataro in GSM blends.

classic_regions.name: Bandol
classic_regions.markers: Bandol rosé: structured, ageworthy, Mourvèdre-led.

confused_with.tell: Syrah has more pepper and violet and less game.
Tannat has even more tannin and higher acid, less garrigue.

carignan.name: Carignan
carignan.markers: Deep colour with high acid and tannin; rustic, spicy; best from old vines.

red.oak: Varies; old vines often concrete or old wood; carbonic maceration in Languedoc.
red.markers: High acid, high tannin, deep colour, rustic red and black fruit.

classic_regions.name: Corbières
classic_regions.markers: Old-vine Languedoc Carignan: rustic, spicy, garrigue.

classic_regions.name: Priorat
classic_regions.markers: Cariñena (Samsó) in Priorat blends adds acid and colour.

classic_regions.name: Montsant
classic_regions.markers: Montsant: Garnacha and Cariñena on varied soils.

classic_regions.name: Carignano del Sulcis
classic_regions.markers: Carignano del Sulcis (Sardinia): ungrafted sand-rooted old vines, plush and spicy.

classic_regions.name: Valle del Maule
classic_regions.markers: VIGNO: Vignadores de Carignan, old dry-farmed Maule vines, minimum 65% Carignan, 30-year-old vines.

cinsault.name: Cinsault
cinsault.markers: Pale, light, perfumed red fruit; rosé partner; Pinotage parent.

red.markers: Pale, light, soft tannin, perfumed red fruit.

classic_regions.name: Swartland
classic_regions.markers: Old-vine Cape Cinsault: pale, perfumed, light and juicy.

classic_regions.name: Valle del Itata
classic_regions.markers: Itata: dry-farmed old vines on granite, light and bright.

classic_regions.name: Bekaa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Château Musar blends with Cabernet and Carignan.

classic_regions.name: Côtes de Provence
classic_regions.markers: Provence rosé: adds freshness and delicacy to Grenache.

classic_regions.name: Clairette du Languedoc
classic_regions.markers: Clairette du Languedoc: soft, herbal, oxidises easily; also rancio style.

classic_regions.name: Clairette de Die
classic_regions.markers: Clairette de Die Méthode Dioise Ancestrale: min 75% Muscat, the rest Clairette; single fermentation stopped by chilling, filtered and rebottled; sweet, grapey, about 7 to 9% abv.

classic_regions.name: Picpoul de Pinet
classic_regions.markers: Picpoul de Pinet: crisp, lemony, saline, by the Thau lagoon oyster beds.

vermentino.name: Vermentino
vermentino.markers: Citrus, herbs, saline, bitter almond finish; coastal Mediterranean.

white.markers: Citrus and herbs, saline, bitter almond finish.

classic_regions.name: Vermentino di Gallura
classic_regions.markers: Sardinia's only DOCG: granite, fuller, saline with a bitter almond finish.

classic_regions.name: Colli di Luni
classic_regions.markers: Liguria and Tuscan coast: herbal, saline.

classic_regions.name: Patrimonio
classic_regions.markers: Corsica (Vermentinu): Patrimonio on limestone.

classic_regions.name: Côtes de Provence
classic_regions.markers: Rolle in Provence whites.

classic_regions.name: Ajaccio
classic_regions.markers: Ajaccio (granite): pale, peppery, herbal Sciaccarellu.

classic_regions.name: Ajaccio
classic_regions.markers: Peppery Corsican rosé.

classic_regions.name: Côtes de Provence
classic_regions.markers: Clos Cibonne: Tibouren rosé, savoury, earthy, aged under voile in old foudres.

red.markers: Teinturier with red juice: opaque colour, soft acid.

classic_regions.name: Alentejo
classic_regions.markers: Alentejo: teinturier (red flesh), dense, dark and rich; Mouchão is the benchmark.

petite-sirah.name: Petite Sirah
petite-sirah.markers: Inky, very tannic, blueberry and black pepper (Durif).

red.markers: Durif: opaque colour, very high tannin.

classic_regions.name: Lodi
classic_regions.markers: Lodi and Napa: inky, tannic, blueberry and pepper.

classic_regions.name: Napa Valley
classic_regions.markers: Old field-blend vineyards.

nebbiolo.name: Nebbiolo
nebbiolo.markers: Pale garnet with orange rim, very high tannin, high acid, high alcohol; tar and roses, sour cherry, liquorice; truffle and leather with age.

red.oak: Traditional: long ageing in large Slavonian oak botti (2,000 to 10,000 l+); modernist: French barriques, 1980s to 2000s; many now combine.
red.markers: Pale garnet colour with an orange or brick rim even when young; high acid; very high, drying tannin; high alcohol; tar, roses, cherry, liquorice; truffle and leather with age.

classic_regions.name: Barolo
classic_regions.markers: Pale garnet with orange rim even young; tar and roses, sour cherry, liquorice; very high tannin and acid; 14 to 15% abv; min 38 months ageing (18 in wood), riserva 62.

classic_regions.name: Cannubi
classic_regions.markers: Barolo village: Cannubi mixes Tortonian (La Morra side) and Serravallian soils; perfumed and balanced.

classic_regions.name: Brunate
classic_regions.markers: La Morra and Barolo: Tortonian marl, perfumed, softer, earlier-drinking.

classic_regions.name: Vignarionda
classic_regions.markers: Serralunga d'Alba: Serravallian (Helvetian) sandstone and limestone, the most powerful, tannic and long-lived.

classic_regions.name: Monprivato
classic_regions.markers: Castiglione Falletto: balance of power and perfume (Mascarello).

classic_regions.name: Ginestra
classic_regions.markers: Monforte d'Alba: dense, structured, long-lived.

classic_regions.name: Barbaresco
classic_regions.markers: Closer to the Tanaro, slightly warmer, earlier harvest: more approachable, finer, often a touch lighter; min 26 months (9 in wood), riserva 50; 12.5% abv min.

classic_regions.name: Valtellina Superiore
classic_regions.markers: Chiavennasca on south-facing Alpine terraces in Lombardy: lighter, fresher, more austere, red fruit and herbs, lower alcohol (12.5 to 13.5%); subzones Sassella, Grumello, Inferno, Valgella, Maroggia.

classic_regions.name: Sforzato di Valtellina
classic_regions.markers: Sforzato (Sfurzat): dried-grape (appassimento) Valtellina, dry, 14%+ abv.

classic_regions.name: Gattinara
classic_regions.markers: Alto Piemonte (Spanna): volcanic porphyry, acidic soils; higher acid, more iron and minerality, lighter body; up to 10% Vespolina and Uva Rara.

classic_regions.name: Ghemme
classic_regions.markers: Ghemme: glacial moraine, softer, with Vespolina.

classic_regions.name: Roero
classic_regions.markers: Sandy Roero (left bank of the Tanaro): lighter, perfumed, softer tannin, earlier drinking.

classic_regions.name: Langhe
classic_regions.markers: Langhe Nebbiolo: younger vines and declassified fruit, approachable.

red.note: Nebbiolo is relatively low in the more stable anthocyanins, which is why its colour is light and turns brick-orange early.

confused_with.tell: Pinot is also pale, but has soft tannin and lower alcohol.
Sangiovese is ruby, sour cherry and dried herbs, less tannin, less floral.
Grenache is pale but low acid and soft tannin.
Xinomavro shares the pale colour, high acid and tannin, with tomato and olive.

sangiovese.name: Sangiovese
sangiovese.markers: Sour cherry, tomato leaf, dried herbs, leather; high acid, high tannin, medium body; ruby to garnet.

red.oak: Traditional large Slavonian botti; modern barriques; Brunello needs at least 2 years in wood.
red.markers: Medium ruby to garnet; high acid; high, sometimes rustic tannin; sour cherry, red plum, tomato leaf, dried oregano and tea; leather and earth with age.

classic_regions.name: Chianti Classico
classic_regions.markers: Sour cherry, violet, dried herbs and tomato leaf; high acid; firm, dusty tannin; galestro and alberese soils; Gran Selezione to be min 90% Sangiovese from 2027 vintage.

classic_regions.name: Panzano
classic_regions.markers: Conca d'Oro of Panzano: warm amphitheatre, rich and ripe.

classic_regions.name: Radda
classic_regions.markers: Radda: high, cool, galestro: bright, sleek, perfumed.

classic_regions.name: Castelnuovo Berardenga
classic_regions.markers: Castelnuovo Berardenga: southern, warmer, fuller and riper.

classic_regions.name: Brunello di Montalcino
classic_regions.markers: 100% Sangiovese (Brunello clone): fuller, richer, more tannic and long-lived; released from 1 January of the fifth year after harvest with at least 2 years in oak (riserva a year later).

classic_regions.name: Montosoli
classic_regions.markers: North-facing Montosoli: cooler, perfumed, elegant.

classic_regions.name: Rosso di Montalcino
classic_regions.markers: Rosso di Montalcino: young-vine, earlier-release version.

classic_regions.name: Vino Nobile di Montepulciano
classic_regions.markers: Prugnolo Gentile (min 70%): softer, more rustic than Brunello; Pieve subzone labelling introduced in the 2020s.

classic_regions.name: Morellino di Scansano
classic_regions.markers: Maremma coast: riper, softer.

classic_regions.name: Carmignano
classic_regions.markers: Carmignano: requires 10 to 20% Cabernet Sauvignon or Franc; one of the zones delimited by Cosimo III in 1716.

classic_regions.name: Bolgheri
classic_regions.markers: Coast: used in Super Tuscans with Bordeaux varieties.

classic_regions.name: Romagna
classic_regions.markers: Sangiovese di Romagna: lighter, juicier; sottozone (MGAs) such as Modigliana and Predappio.

classic_regions.name: Montecucco Sangiovese
classic_regions.markers: Montecucco: warm, between Montalcino and the sea.

classic_regions.name: Chianti Rùfina
classic_regions.markers: Chianti Rùfina: high, cool, structured, ageworthy.

classic_regions.name: Tuscany
classic_regions.markers: Tuscan rosato.

confused_with.tell: Nebbiolo is paler with more tannin, tar and roses.
Tempranillo has lower acid, more tobacco and leather, and American oak.
Aglianico is darker with more tannin, smoke and black fruit.

barbera.name: Barbera
barbera.markers: Deep ruby with high acid and low tannin; cherry and plum.

red.oak: Unoaked (fruity, acidic) or barrique-aged (the 1980s modernist style of Bricco dell'Uccellone softened acid and added tannin).
red.markers: Deep colour, high acid, low tannin: the defining combination; sour and black cherry.

classic_regions.name: Barbera d'Asti
classic_regions.markers: Barbera d'Asti: brighter, fresher, higher acid, red cherry.

classic_regions.name: Nizza
classic_regions.markers: Nizza DOCG (2014): 100% Barbera, riper, oaked, the top Asti tier.

classic_regions.name: Barbera d'Alba
classic_regions.markers: Barbera d'Alba: fuller, richer, from Barolo-zone soils.

classic_regions.name: Barbera del Monferrato Superiore
classic_regions.markers: Monferrato: lighter, sometimes frizzante.

classic_regions.name: Mendoza
classic_regions.markers: Italian-immigrant plantings in Mendoza.

confused_with.tell: Dolcetto has more tannin and lower acid, with bitter almond.
Sangiovese has much more tannin.

dolcetto.name: Dolcetto
dolcetto.markers: Deep purple, low acid, firm tannin, bitter almond finish.

red.markers: Deep purple, low to medium acid, medium+ tannin, black cherry and bitter almond finish.

classic_regions.name: Dogliani
classic_regions.markers: Dogliani DOCG: the fullest, longest-lived Dolcetto.

classic_regions.name: Dolcetto di Diano d'Alba
classic_regions.markers: Diano d'Alba: sorì (sunny sites) on the label.

classic_regions.name: Dolcetto d'Alba
classic_regions.markers: Dolcetto d'Alba: everyday Langhe red.

classic_regions.name: Dolcetto di Ovada Superiore
classic_regions.markers: Ovada: firmer.

freisa.name: Freisa
freisa.markers: Raspberry and rose with high acid and tannin; Nebbiolo relative.

classic_regions.name: Freisa d'Asti
classic_regions.markers: Freisa d'Asti: dry or slightly sweet, sometimes frizzante; high acid and tannin.

grignolino.name: Grignolino
grignolino.markers: Pale yet tannic; strawberry and pepper.

red.markers: Very pale but tannic (many pips).

classic_regions.name: Grignolino d'Asti
classic_regions.markers: Pale, tannic, peppery Piedmont curiosity.

ruche.name: Ruché
ruche.markers: Aromatic red: rose, geranium and pepper.

classic_regions.name: Ruchè di Castagnole Monferrato
classic_regions.markers: Ruchè di Castagnole Monferrato DOCG: aromatic red, rose and pepper.

arneis.name: Arneis
arneis.markers: Pear and almond, soft acid; Roero.

classic_regions.name: Roero
classic_regions.markers: Roero Arneis: pear, almond and flowers, soft acid, on sandy soil.

classic_regions.name: Gavi
classic_regions.markers: Gavi (Gavi di Gavi from the commune of Gavi): crisp, lemon, delicate, almond.

timorasso.name: Timorasso
timorasso.markers: Full yet high acid, mineral, ages with petrol-like notes.

classic_regions.name: Colli Tortonesi
classic_regions.markers: Derthona (Colli Tortonesi): rich, mineral, ageworthy; Walter Massa's revival.

glera.name: Glera
glera.markers: Pear, green apple and flowers; light; tank-method Prosecco.

sparkling.markers: Light, low to medium acid, simple pear, green apple and white flowers; tank method, no autolysis; often Extra Dry (12 to 17 g/l).

classic_regions.name: Conegliano Valdobbiadene - Prosecco
classic_regions.markers: Conegliano Valdobbiadene DOCG: steep hills; Rive (single communes or hamlets) and Cartizze (107 ha); tank (Martinotti or Charmat) method.

classic_regions.name: Colli Asolani - Prosecco
classic_regions.markers: Asolo Prosecco DOCG.

classic_regions.name: Prosecco
classic_regions.markers: Prosecco DOC (nine provinces, Veneto and Friuli): simple, fruity; Prosecco Rosé since 2020 (with Pinot Nero).

confused_with.tell: Traditional-method Chardonnay shows biscuit and higher acid.
Moscato d'Asti is grapier and sweeter, lower alcohol.

corvina.name: Corvina
corvina.markers: Sour cherry and bitter almond (Valpolicella); raisin, chocolate and high alcohol (Amarone).

red.markers: Light, sour cherry, bitter almond.

classic_regions.name: Valpolicella
classic_regions.markers: Valpolicella Classico: light, sour cherry, almond.

classic_regions.name: Bardolino
classic_regions.markers: Bardolino (and Chiaretto rosé): lighter still.

red_dried.label: Appassimento (Amarone)
red_dried.oak: Amarone: min 2 years ageing (4 for riserva), in large botti or barriques.
red_dried.markers: Dried-fruit, raisin and chocolate with very high alcohol, full body and a bitter (amaro) finish.

classic_regions.name: Amarone della Valpolicella
classic_regions.markers: Grapes dried (appassimento) for about 3 to 4 months; dry or near-dry, 15 to 17% abv, raisin, dried cherry, chocolate, full body, high alcohol.

classic_regions.name: Valpolicella Ripasso
